newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Strong dollar propels Dutch shares to record close.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar propels Dutch shares to record close.

text.p: Dutch shares extended their winning streak on Tuesday as a stronger dollar and a further fall in bond yields propelled the market to another new high.
The AEX closed 9.13 points firmer at 636.37, bettering the previous closing high from last Friday by more than five points.

Dealers said investors kept piling into the share market, even though the AEX has already risen more than 30 percent this year, because yields on fixed-interest instruments were too low to provide an attractive alternative.
The Amsterdam market, one of the most dollar-sensitive in Europe, drew strength from the U.S. currency's rise to levels around 1.7575 guilders today from 1.7290 late on Monday.
Supermarkets group Ahold, with over half of its sales generated in the U.S., was one of the main beneficiaries, closing 2.10 guilders firmer at 107.10.
Chemicals group Akzo Nobel was another outperformer, jumping 5.50 guilders to 232.00.
Among losing issues, temporary employment agency Randstad stood out, sliding 6.80 guilders or over five percent to 125.20.
The shares were hit by a newspaper report that a union was urging Randstad to change the way it pays temporary workers and that this could reduce its margins by up to two percent.
